title: Huxhold et al. (2014): Multiple Choice
instructions: Choose the answer that best preserves the study design, coefficient patterns, and limits of interpretation.

items.prompt: Which conclusion best captures the study's main pattern of findings?
options: Activity frequency alone explained well-being, regardless of the social partner
Associations differed by partner source, age group, and aspect of well-being
Family-friend differences appeared only in middle age and disappeared among older adults
Friend activities were linked only to life satisfaction and never to positive or negative affect
items.answer: Associations differed by partner source, age group, and aspect of well-being
items.explanation: The study distinguishes family and friend activities and examines life satisfaction, positive affect (PA), and negative affect (NA) separately. It does not treat all activity as one uniform benefit.

items.prompt: Which contrast between family and friendship relationships underlies the study?
options: Families provide companionship exclusively, whereas friends provide only instrumental support
The functions are identical, but only family ties can be voluntarily ended
Friendship is maintained by obligation, whereas family ties depend entirely on voluntary choice
Family ties carry obligations; friendships emphasize choice, reciprocity, and companionship
items.answer: Family ties carry obligations; friendships emphasize choice, reciprocity, and companionship
items.explanation: The authors discuss structural and functional differences, including the greater difficulty of dissolving unsatisfying family ties. They do not assign each type of relationship one exclusive function.

options: Older adults would be less active, with a larger age difference in friend activities
Older adults would be more active, with a larger age difference in family activities
Activity levels would be identical, although friend activity alone would rise in old age
Only relationship quality would differ by age, with no differences in activity levels
items.answer: Older adults would be less active, with a larger age difference in friend activities
items.explanation: H1 combined a general prediction of lower activity among older adults with a particularly pronounced difference in activities with friends.

items.prompt: Which combination correctly identifies the data used and final analysis groups?
options: Germany, 1996 and 2002: 2,032 middle-aged and 2,830 older adults
Germany, 2002 and 2008: only 4,862 participants with complete data at both waves
Germany, 2002 and 2008: 2,830 middle-aged and 2,032 older adults
Germany, 2002 only: 1,327 middle-aged and 665 older adults
items.answer: Germany, 2002 and 2008: 2,830 middle-aged and 2,032 older adults
items.explanation: The study used two German Aging Survey waves. Only 1,327 middle-aged and 665 older adults participated at both waves; full-information maximum likelihood retained available information beyond these complete follow-up cases.

items.prompt: Why use latent change score (LCS) models for the main research question?
options: To average both waves and test only cross-sectional age-group differences
To relate baseline activity to subsequent well-being change while accounting for initial levels
To remove every unmeasured confounder and identify an experimental causal effect
To discard all incomplete cases before comparing raw change scores
items.answer: To relate baseline activity to subsequent well-being change while accounting for initial levels
items.explanation: LCS separates the T1 level from T1-to-T2 change and estimates associations between initial activity and six-year change in well-being. Change-to-change associations were included but were not interpreted as directional evidence.

items.prompt: Why could the researchers not directly contrast regression weights between age groups?
options: Factor loadings changed over time, preventing a consistent measurement model
Unequal sample sizes made any multigroup analysis mathematically impossible
The models omitted every baseline association between activity and well-being
Variances of the change scores could not be constrained equal across groups
items.answer: Variances of the change scores could not be constrained equal across groups
items.explanation: Factor loadings supported invariance between measurement occasions. However, equality of change variances across age groups was not supported, limiting direct between-group comparisons of regression weights.
items.source: A limit on age-group coefficient comparisons

items.prompt: Which result describes activity change among older adults from 2002 to 2008?
options: Friend activity declined while family activity increased significantly
Only friend activity declined; family activity remained unchanged in both groups
Family activity declined more than friend activity
Friend activity rose in middle age while family activity rose in old age
items.answer: Family activity declined more than friend activity
items.explanation: The age-group-by-time interaction was significant for family activity but not friend activity. The within-period decline is distinct from the larger between-group difference in friend activity levels.

items.prompt: Which summary matches the middle-aged group's results?
options: Activity predicted PA and life-satisfaction gains, with no NA link or significant source difference
Family activity predicted only PA, whereas friend activity predicted only life satisfaction
Both activity sources predicted increases in all three outcomes, but only family coefficients were significant
Activity predicted only declining NA and was unrelated to PA or life satisfaction
items.answer: Activity predicted PA and life-satisfaction gains, with no NA link or significant source difference
items.explanation: The standardized coefficients were 0.08 for PA and 0.08 for life satisfaction; the NA coefficient was 0.01 and nonsignificant. Family-friend contrasts were not significant.

items.prompt: What was found for positive affect in the older group?
options: Only friend activity predicted PA; the family association was absent
The common coefficient was positive, with no significant family-friend difference
Family activity predicted PA gains while friend activity predicted PA losses
Neither activity source predicted PA change after baseline levels were considered
items.answer: The common coefficient was positive, with no significant family-friend difference
items.explanation: The common standardized coefficient for PA was 0.09. Allowing separate family and friend weights did not reveal a significant source difference.

items.prompt: Which coefficients and interpretation match older adults' life-satisfaction results?
options: Friends: 0.02; family: 0.14; only family activity predicted change
Friends and family: 0.09; their weights did not differ
Friends: -0.08; family: +0.08; their associations canceled
Friends: 0.14; family: 0.02; only friend activity predicted change
items.answer: Friends: 0.14; family: 0.02; only friend activity predicted change
items.explanation: Releasing the equality constraint improved model fit. In this model, baseline friend activity predicted life-satisfaction change, whereas family activity did not.

items.prompt: According to the older-group results prose, which pattern was reported for negative affect?
options: Friends and family both had coefficients of -0.08
Friends had a coefficient of +0.14 and family of +0.02
Friends: -0.08; family: +0.08, indicating opposite directions
The source coefficients differed but both were effectively zero
items.explanation: The results prose links friend activity to decreasing NA and family activity to increasing NA, so a common coefficient obscures opposing directions. This answer follows that prose. Table 1 reverses the signs in the family and friend rows, creating an unresolved text-table discrepancy.

items.prompt: How should the evidence for Hypothesis 2 be judged?
options: Partial support: beneficial associations did not imply a uniform advantage for friends
Complete support: friend activity was superior for every outcome in both age groups
Complete rejection: no activity-well-being association appeared in either age group
Support confined to a friend advantage in middle age, regardless of older-adult findings
items.answer: Partial support: beneficial associations did not imply a uniform advantage for friends
items.explanation: The H2 discussion notes benefits of shared leisure activity in middle age, but no advantage for friends over family in that group. Positive activity associations and a stronger friend effect are separate parts of the hypothesis.

items.prompt: Which interpretation respects the causal limits of the design?
options: Baseline activity predicted later well-being change, proving a causal effect
Baseline activity predicted later change, but the design does not establish causation
Two-wave data contain no temporal ordering and cannot support directional associations
Covariate adjustment eliminated every unmeasured confounder and all reverse influences
items.answer: Baseline activity predicted later change, but the design does not establish causation
items.explanation: The models estimate directional associations from T1 activity to later well-being change while considering baseline and reciprocal associations. The study did not randomly assign social activities.

items.prompt: Which set of limitations did the authors identify?
options: PA and NA were combined into one scale after partners had been distinguished
Relationship quality was measured, but activity frequency and age were not
Self-report, two widely spaced waves, and limited detail on family ties and relationship quality
Random assignment was successful, but the experimental group lacked long-term follow-up
items.answer: Self-report, two widely spaced waves, and limited detail on family ties and relationship quality
items.explanation: Recall may depend on current affect. Two waves six years apart can miss shorter-term dynamics. Different family relationships and the quality of family or friendship ties were not distinguished in the analyses.

items.prompt: Which practical implication do the authors draw?
options: Support opportunities to build and maintain voluntary friendship networks in later life
Reorganize informal activity around family alone and reduce older adults' friend contacts
Increase contact frequency uniformly without considering partners or emotional consequences
Assume the same intervention effect for every older adult from the observed associations
items.answer: Support opportunities to build and maintain voluntary friendship networks in later life
items.explanation: The conclusion suggests friend-based networks and examples such as volunteering, cultural, university, and occupational-therapy programs. These are implications; this survey study did not itself test their intervention effects.
